name: Cafés and coffee shops
shape_facts: Number of outlets and whether beans are roasted in-house or bought from a roaster
Food offering: pastries bought in, baked on site, or a full brunch kitchen
Seating vs grab-and-go share, and any drive-thru or kiosk
Opening hours and peak windows (morning commute, afternoon, late night)
Delivery-app presence and share of orders
Equipment owned vs leased (espresso machine, grinders)
Whether the owner works the bar
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems: milk and pastry wastage, bean and cup stock, barista consistency and turnover, slow queues, loyalty, laptop sitters, delivery apps and cash. It does not give food-safety, allergen, caffeine-health or licensing advice, nor tax or lease- law advice. It does not store customer names, numbers or loyalty data, staff details, or payment details, and records issues by role.

vocabulary.dial in: adjusting grind and recipe each morning
vocabulary.single origin: beans from one farm or region
vocabulary.karak: strong, sweet milk tea popular in the Gulf
vocabulary.par: how much of an item should be in stock

wastage: What gets binned most at closing — pastries, milk or something else?
costing: Do you know roughly what each drink costs you to make?
When did you last change prices?
consistency: Do customers notice a difference between baristas?
How are recipes shared with new staff?
staff: How long do baristas usually stay?
What makes them leave, from what you hear?
queue: What time is the busiest rush?
Where does the line get stuck?
customers: Do you know who your regulars are?
How do you reward them now?
supply: How often do you run low before the next delivery?
cash: Is the closing gap in cash or card?
delivery: What share of orders come through apps?
What do app complaints usually say?
marketing: Where do new customers find you?
reporting: How do you see the day’s sales if you’re not there?

seasons: - PK: winter is peak café season; Ramadan flips trade to post-iftar and late night; university exams fill seats; summer heat pushes iced drinks and evening trade; Independence Day and New Year events in malls. - UAE: October–April outdoor season is strongest; Ramadan evenings very late; summer pushes traffic into malls and delivery; school and university terms shape weekday mornings. - Canada: autumn and winter boost hot drinks and seasonal specials; summer iced drinks and patios; university terms and exam weeks; December holiday gift cards and bean gifting.
care: Burns from steam wands, slips, electrical faults or a customer collapsing: pi points to emergency services first.
Allergen or dairy-alternative questions from customers: pi notes the operational process issue only, no health advice.
Caffeine and health claims for menu items: pi does not advise.
Loyalty or customer lists: pi never collects customer phone numbers or names.
Barista theft suspicion: noted by pattern and role, no covert monitoring advice.
Lease and rent disputes: noted as a cost problem, no legal advice.
Requests to write fake reviews or bulk-follow schemes: pi declines.
build_ideas: Cost-per-cup calculator for every drink, linked to latest bean, milk and cup prices
Daily wastage log on a tablet for pastries and milk, with weekly trend by item
Par-level stock list for milks, beans, syrups and cups with reorder alerts via WhatsApp
Recipe cards with photos and target shot/milk measures for each drink
Digital loyalty using phone number at the counter, with stamp history and abuse checks
End-of-day WhatsApp summary: sales by hour, top drinks, wastage, cash vs card
WhatsApp or web pre-order flow for office runs with ready-time slots
Barista rota and swap requests on phone
Wholesale bean customer ledger with invoice reminders
Equipment service log with due dates and supplier contacts
Free-drink and staff-meal log by shift
Two-outlet comparison view: sales by hour, average ticket, wastage

exchange.text: honestly my main issue is pastries. we throw out so many every night.
Noted — a lot of pastries end up binned at closing. Are they baked in-house or bought in from a bakery?
Got it, noted. Who decides how many to order each day?
Thanks, noted that the order is a daily guess. Is it the same quantity every day, or do you change it for weekends?
